diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed PF1, PF2, and PF3 via proper reveal actions, and all four settled without hitting the turn cap. The gate failed because rollouts 1 and 2 exhibited an ENCODING MISMATCH: the settling agent (A1) emitted the settlement with decision fields flattened to the top level instead of nested under a "decisions" key (as rollouts 0 and 3 did). When the settlement lacked the "decisions" wrapper, the extraction pipeline recorded empty credited_facts, empty commitments, and empty justification_fact_ids, causing every content check (C1, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7) and provenance check (P1) to fail despite the decision values themselves being correct in rollout 1. In rollout 2, the decision field values additionally omitted facility and personnel details (RP-2, CB-1, Sgt. Lee/RV-17), placing them only in commitments, and two early turns produced unparsable JSON (turns 1-2), extending the conversation to 9 turns—though all facts were eventually re-revealed correctly.

fix_instructions: The primary failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH driven by inconsistent settlement schema. (1) Tighten the settle-eligibility instruction or settlement schema validation to require a nested "decisions" object—rollouts 0 and 3 passed precisely because they used {"settlement": {"decisions": {...}, "credited_facts": [...], "justification_fact_ids": [...]}} while rollouts 1 and 2 flattened decisions to the top level and lost all metadata. (2) For C1, C5 (gated by PF1): ensure the extraction reads settlement.decisions.engineering_window and requires PF1 in justification_fact_ids; in rollout 1 the value was correct but justification_fact_ids was empty due to the schema mismatch, and in rollout 2 the value omitted "reinforced pad RP-2" entirely. (3) For C2, C6, P1 (gated by PF2): same pattern—rollout 1 had the correct value but empty justification_fact_ids, and rollout 2 omitted "climate-controlled bay CB-1" from the decision field. (4) For C3, C7 (gated by PF3): rollout 1 had the correct value but empty justification_fact_ids; rollout 2 omitted "Sgt. Lee" and "RV-17" from the decision field. (5) Additionally, reinforce in the settlement instructions that facility assignments (RP-2, CB-1) and personnel/vehicle names (Sgt. Lee, RV-17) must appear in the decision field values themselves, not only in commitments, to prevent the rollout-2 pattern where details migrate to commitments. (6) The unparsable JSON in rollout 2 turns 1-2 suggests adding a JSON validation retry or stricter output-format guidance for reveal actions, though this did not prevent eventual disclosure.
